description: Everything for a 10-K / 10-Q case in ONE call, already cited: the company and the filing (form, accession, period, filed date), this period against the prior comparable period (`compare_periods`, with `derived_id`s), key ratios, earnings signals, forensic flags (`forensic_audit`), the company's restatements, and the filing-section index with the exact `read_filing_section` arguments for MD&A and Risk Factors. Each section is the underlying tool's output unchanged (`value`, `fact_id` / `derived_id`, `availability`, `metrics_display`): quote it verbatim. A section above the caller's plan, or that fails, carries its own `status` and error and sets `degraded: true`; it never fails the pack and is never shown as empty. Point-in-time: with `as_of_date` (or an explicit `accession` / `period`, which cuts at that filing's acceptance date) every section reads only what was knowable then; the forensic audit has no as-of date, so it is not run in a dated case. Start here for a filing case, then read the sections you need. Each section keeps the plan gate of its own tool.

accession.description: A specific 10-K / 10-Q to review. Omit for the latest.

as_of_date.description: Point-in-time cutoff: every section reads only what the SEC had accepted by this date. A section that cannot honour it is not run and says so.

ticker.description: Company ticker or CIK (SEC identifier), e.g. 'AAPL' or '0000320193'. A CIK is the stable identifier.

name: get_filing_review_pack

_meta.description: Response metadata (provenance, point-in-time flag, freshness, request id and warnings). Every field is documented once in the agent contract (agent_contract.meta in the server's manifest.json).

degraded.description: True when any section did not return its data. Read each section's `status`; an unreadable section is never an empty one.

title: Filing Review Pack
